summary: The round-7 blocker is genuinely closed and closed on NEW ground: measured in my own tree, replacing the checkpoint hop's `upTo` with `Long.MAX_VALUE` (ChainReplay.java:255) now fails exactly one test -- theBOUNDEDCrossingStillStopsAtTheSlotTheCONTINUENamed -- and it fails for the right reason (expected 1L but was 2L, the zombie folded in), which also PROVES the fixture's checkpoint is ACCEPTED and the bounded hop reached, since a mutation confined to the checkpoint hop could not otherwise change the result. It does not re-cover its sibling: deleting the barrier guard (`checkpoint.sequence() - 1 > upTo`) fails only aCheckpointCoveringEntriesPASTTheBarrierIsNotUsed, and widening the hop fails only the new test. The two round-8 assertion edits are `.as()` labels added to existing exact equalities -- no rule 4/5 weakening in this delta. BUT the asymmetry hunt the round asked for finds the SAME invariant still unnetted at its sibling call site: `crossFromCheckpoint` is called from three places with three different barriers, and only the FIRST-hop call (line 129) now has a test. Widening the in-loop CONTINUE-branch call (line 163) to Long.MAX_VALUE leaves the ENTIRE build green, and I measured it folding a fenced ancestor's discarded suffix into a takeover's offsets (1 -> 2) on the shape the row itself calls the common case. The new test's own comment says the barrier is 'constructed twice'; it is reached from three sites, and that undercount is why one is still open. One further minor: the M4.9-added `chainEpoch == ownEpoch` guard survives deletion across the whole build, where its pre-existing twin in applyChain is killed by CommitLogCrossEpochTest.

findings.summary: The new test nets the FIRST-HOP barrier only. `crossFromCheckpoint` is called from three sites -- ChainReplay.java:129 (first hop, `upTo`), :163 (the walk's own probe after a CONTINUE, `limit`) and :197 (the burned-epoch arithmetic step, where `limit` is Long.MAX_VALUE by construction) -- and the barrier it builds is whatever argument that call passes. MEASURED IN MY OWN TREE, not argued: changing line 163 alone to `crossFromCheckpoint(hops, chainEpoch, Long.MAX_VALUE)` leaves `./gradlew test` BUILD SUCCESSFUL across every module, all 787 tests. Under that mutant a fenced ancestor's discarded suffix IS folded into a successor's inherited offsets: with epoch 1 holding one real delta, a LATEST checkpoint at the barrier and one ZOMBIE delta above it, an UNCHECKPOINTED epoch 2 between (the row's own 'term shorter than K above terms that did checkpoint'), and epoch 3 opening from epoch 2, `successor.nextOffset(streamOfTerm(1))` reads 1 on the staged tree and 2 under the mutant. That is I3, on the path this task adds, and it is the round-7 finding at the sibling call site rather than a new class of defect. The new test's comment ('THE BARRIER IS CONSTRUCTED TWICE SINCE M4.9') undercounts the sites, which is exactly why the second one has no net -- the same stale-inventory shape the commit body catalogues six times.
findings.failure_scenario: A leader at epoch 1 is fenced and keeps committing. Epoch 2 seals it at the slot its CONTINUE names and runs a term too short to checkpoint (K ships at 1000). Epoch 3 takes over from epoch 2: the first-hop probe misses on the uncheckpointed epoch 2, so it is the WALK's in-loop probe that finds epoch 1's checkpoint. Any future edit that loses `limit` at that call -- a refactor to a shared helper, a copy of the first-hop line, or a maintainer who reads the new test and believes the barrier is netted -- applies epoch 1's discarded suffix, re-issuing ACKED offsets to a new stream position. Nothing in the suite says a word.
findings.suggested_fix: Parametrise the new test over the two reachable call sites, or add one sibling that inserts an uncheckpointed intermediate epoch between the checkpointed ancestor and the recovering chain (the fixture above; ~15 lines, same shape as the existing one). The mutation to observe red against is `Long.MAX_VALUE` at ChainReplay.java:163.

findings.summary: The M4.9-added `if (chainEpoch == ownEpoch)` around the checkpoint's `nextSequence` seeding has no test on its FALSE arm. Measured: replacing it with `if (true)` leaves the whole build green (787 tests), and it is NOT an equivalent mutant -- on the `aRunOfBURNEDEpochsStillStopsAtTheCheckpointBehindThem` shape a recovering epoch-4 chain reads nextSequence 1 on the staged tree and 41 under the mutant, i.e. it takes its own next slot from an ANCESTOR's checkpoint and leaves slots 1..40 of its own chain empty. The pre-existing twin of this guard, `hop.epoch() == ownEpoch` in applyChain, IS killed -- `CommitLogCrossEpochTest.aSuccESSORResumesTheStreamWhereItsPredecessorStopped` fails under the same mutation -- so this is the same asymmetry shape as T1, one layer down. Graded MINOR rather than major only because the harmful path is not reachable from production today: `CommitLog.recover()` has exactly one production caller (LocalSequencer.java:301), on a freshly minted, still-empty chain whose walk terminates at the origin before any ancestor cross, and the seeding direction is monotone-forward so it cannot re-race a taken slot. That is the same reachability status as the arm the commit DID pin (`recoveringAChainThatCheckpointedItsOWNProgressKeepsItsNextSequence`, pinned 'because a restart recovering its own chain is exactly that shape').
findings.failure_scenario: A later commit gives `recover()` a second caller on an already-opened chain -- M4.23's origin gap, M4.6d's rerouting, or a restart path -- and the guard is dropped or inverted in a refactor. The chain's next commit lands hundreds of slots past its own last entry, and the production comment fifty lines below ('OFFSETS CROSS, SEQUENCE NUMBERS DO NOT ... would send the successor's first delta past its own empty slots and break the consecutiveness the seal protocol depends on') is the only thing that says this is wrong.
findings.suggested_fix: One assertion on `reader.nextSequence()` in the existing burned-epoch test would kill it; nothing new needs building.
